images.title: The class newsroom wall
images.purpose: Give the whole chapter on one picture: a newsroom wall with four small panels in a row, one for each way of showing data (a table, a pictograph, a bar graph and a picture), for the student to say one idea from each.
images.composition: A title and one wall holding four pinned panels in a row, each with a simple drawing and a label under it: Table, Pictograph, Bar graph and Picture.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Title The class newsroom wall centred at (728, 55) in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). WALL: one rounded rectangle (corner radius 24, construction grey #6B7280 outline 4 px, white fill) x 20 to 1436, y 100 to 670. On it, exactly 4 panels in one row, each a white rounded rectangle 290 px wide and 440 px high (y 140 to 580, corner radius 14, dark #2B2B2B outline 3 px), at x 58 to 348, 408 to 698, 758 to 1048 and 1108 to 1398, each with one reddish purple #CC79A7 pin (a circle of radius 9) at the top centre (y 158). Under each panel, centred on the panel and at y 625, its label in dark #1F2937 bold (44 px): Table, Pictograph, Bar graph and Picture. PANEL 1, Table: a mini table of exactly 3 rows and 2 columns, 220 px wide and 270 px high, x 93 to 313 and y 190 to 460, every cell 110 by 90 px with a dark outline (3 px); each of the 3 left cells holds one amber #E69F00 square (36 px) centred in it, the 3 right cells are empty. PANEL 2, Pictograph: a thin construction grey line (3 px) as a vertical edge at x 436 from y 200 to y 480 and exactly 3 rows of round teal #0072B2 icons (circles of 40 px with a dark outline), centred on y 240, 340 and 440, the icons of a row 52 px apart starting at x 458: row 1 has 2 icons, row 2 has 4 icons, row 3 has 3 icons. PANEL 3, Bar graph: a vertical line (4 px) at x 798 from y 210 to y 500 and a horizontal base (4 px) at y 500 from x 798 to x 1018, with no marks and no numbers; exactly 3 amber #E69F00 bars, each 44 px wide with a dark outline, x 823 to 867 (top at y 370), x 887 to 931 (top at y 290) and x 951 to 995 (top at y 420), all standing on the base. PANEL 4, Picture: exactly 4 small children in two rows of two, head centres at (1203, 235), (1303, 235), (1203, 405) and (1303, 405); every child is a white round head (radius 18) with a dark outline, a grey #6B7280 body 36 by 56 px and two dark legs; the two children on the left each wear an amber #E69F00 hat (a triangle 30 px wide), the two children on the right each hold a teal #0072B2 flag on a thin pole. No number is written in any panel. In all there are 4 panels, 4 labels, 4 pins and 1 title. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 4 panels, or panels in an order other than Table, Pictograph, Bar graph, Picture
any number, total, scale or answer written inside a panel
a mini table without 3 rows, a mini bar graph without 3 bars, or a picture panel without 4 children
images.takeaway: Data can be recorded in a table, a pictograph, a bar graph or a picture, and each shows the same kind of facts in its own way.
images.description: A newsroom wall with four panels in a row: a small table of 3 rows, a small pictograph of 3 rows of icons, a small bar graph of 3 bars and a small group of 4 children.
images.context: Concept image for Chapter Revision: Data Through Pictures. It gathers the ways of showing data in your maths book into one map; the panels are only reminders, so they carry no numbers.
images.teaching_notes: Walk the wall from left to right and ask the student to say one idea at each panel: how a table is read, what an icon stands for, what a bar's height tells and how a picture is counted. Do not add numbers to the panels.

image_decisions.why: A wall of four small panels gives the revision one picture to walk through, with a table, a pictograph, a bar graph and a picture.
